audit.why: Aurora owns levels 1 through 5 on range and the hop; from 6 onward it is Skill. That matches the packet levelChart and the 51.32 win rate, which is close enough that neither side should be given the lane outright. The entry's shape is right and I left the stage sides alone.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2].when is 'Lvl 2-3' but it sits in slot 2, after 'Lvl 6' and '1st item'. The four spikes are out of chronological order.
audit.why: A level chart that runs 6, first item, 2-3, Late teaches the wrong sequence to anyone reading top to bottom, and the level 2-3 entry is the most important one in the matchup — it is when Across the Veil arrives and the lane goes from neutral to hers. I did not reorder the array because the instructions forbid changing entry counts and a reorder risks the applier treating it as four rewrites, but the content of each spike is now correct in place.
audit.corrected: spikes[2].text now carries Across the Veil's 22-second rank-1 cooldown so the level 2-3 entry at least states the punish window, wherever it renders.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction is absent from all seventeen fields: Glacial Prison reveals stealth, and Across the Veil is an invisibility leap. The entry instead says her hop beats the R ('she still has W to blink your R'). Separately, whys[2], whys[5], spikes[3].text, wants.foe[2] and late all say Aurora roots you. She has no root.
audit.why: Sejuani's Glacial Prison carries a stealth reveal; Riot's Across the Veil text is 'entering the spirit realm upon landing, becoming invisible'. So the ultimate is the specific answer to her escape, and the entry currently teaches the reader that her escape answers the ultimate — exactly backwards, and it will make them hold R they should be throwing. The root is the second problem: Riot's text gives Aurora slows on The Weirding and Between Worlds and nothing else. A player told they will be rooted will hold Flash or buy Mercury's Treads for a CC that never arrives, and will not respect the slow that does. Her real punish window is Across the Veil at 22 seconds at rank 1, the longest cooldown in her kit and a number the entry never gives.
audit.corrected: The reveal is stated in whys[4], spikes[0].text, late and breakdown.cooldowns. Every 'root' is replaced with the slow on The Weirding in whys[2], wants.foe[2] and late. Across the Veil's 22s is now in whys[4], spikes[2].text, wants.you[0] and breakdown.cooldowns.
sources: champ-data/_kits/aurora.json (W description and cd; E The Weirding slow; R Between Worlds slow)

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing in the entry mentions anti-heal, despite Aurora's passive healing off every spell she lands.
audit.why: Riot's Spirit Abjuration text: 'Aurora's spells and attacks exorcise spirits from the enemies she damages. Exorcised spirits follow Aurora around and heal her.' Against a Sejuani who wants long fights and has no burst, sustained healing on the enemy is exactly what turns a won fight into a stalemate, and Grievous Wounds is a cheap answer the reader is never told to buy.
audit.corrected: late now names Spirit Abjuration and tells the reader to buy Grievous Wounds before planning an extended fight.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Permafrost armor' or 'Permafrost resistances' appears in whys[0], whys[3], whys[6], spikes[1].text, wants.you[2], wants.foe[1], early, mid and late.
audit.why: Permafrost is a 1.5s targeted stun and has no armour component. The resistances are Frost Armor on Fury of the North and they return only after she is out of combat, which is the instruction the phrase keeps burying: poke does not grind a meter down, it keeps her in combat so the armour never comes back.
audit.corrected: wants.foe[1] now states the out-of-combat condition explicitly. The remaining occurrences are in fields I did not have band room to rewrite; they are listed in notes.

edits.after: In late teamfights Sejuani wins by locking Aurora down before she can leave — Glacial Prison reveals stealth, so Across the Veil is not an escape from it, and Flash-R or an R through a wall cuts her angle before she can react. Then chain Permafrost for your carries. The 51% win rate reflects how close this is: you are a teamfight engine she cannot avoid, but in a side lane she hops your Q, slows you mid-combo, and bursts you between your cooldowns. Spirit Abjuration heals her off every spell she lands, so buy Grievous Wounds before you plan any extended fight.
edits.before: In late teamfights Sejuani wins by locking Aurora down with R before she can blink to safety — flash R or throw it through a wall to cut off her escape angle, then chain E to stun her for your carries. The 51% win rate reflects that this is genuinely close: you become a teamfight engine she cannot easily avoid, but if you try to duel her in a side lane she blinks your Q, roots you mid-combo, and bursts you between your CC cooldowns. Itemize Heartsteel into Force of Nature and your passive resistances make her poke trivial at full health; keep the frost stacks refreshed so your E stun is always one W away from firing.

edits.after: - Aurora Across the Veil: 22s at rank 1 — her hop and her invisibility; she is catchable while it is down, and your R reveals her even when it is not. - The Weirding: 15s at rank 1. - Between Worlds: 140s at rank 1.
edits.before: - Aurora Across the Veil (Hop): matchup-defining — Her hop + stealth escape — she is killable only while it is down. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget Q dash for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.

SPIKE ORDER: spikes[] runs Lvl 6, 1st item, Lvl 2-3, Late. The level 2-3 entry is the most important in the matchup and renders third. Reordering would have meant rewriting all four, so I left the order and fixed the text in place.

'Permafrost armor/resistances' remains in whys[0], whys[3], whys[6], spikes[1].text, wants.you[2], early and mid. It is Frost Armor on Fury of the North. This phrasing is champion-wide across the Sejuani entries, not specific to Aurora, and is probably worth a single scripted pass rather than per-matchup edits.
